name: Is a pre-approved ADU plan worth using?

mainEntity.name: Is a pre-approved ADU plan worth using if I want a more custom design?
mainEntity.text: Is a pre-approved ADU plan worth using if I want a more custom design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pre-approved plans can be a smart option when the priority is speed, lower design cost, or a more predictable approval path. They are especially useful for homeowners who want a straightforward unit and do not need a highly customized layout. The tradeoff is flexibility. Pre-approved plans may not align with the exact shape of the lot, the preferred aesthetic, or privacy goals. They can also force compromises on window placement, access, and orientation. A custom design is usually better when the site is unusual, the homeowner wants a luxury finish, or the ADU needs to complement a specific main house style. The right choice depends on the property and the owner’s goals. If the lot is simple and the timeline matters, a pre-approved plan may be excellent. If the site is complex or design quality is a priority, customization is usually worth it.
acceptedAnswer.description: A pre-approved plan can save time and simplify approval, but it may not fit your lot, style, or privacy goals as well as a custom design. It is most useful when speed and predictability matter more than architectural flexibility.
